summary: Wooden harbour light at the outer end of the Port Medway breakwater, lit 1899, deactivated in 1987 or 1989, and now the centre of a municipal park since 2002.

light.characteristic: fixed red (1899); green from 1967 (Region of Queens)

structures.type: square wooden tower with sloping sides and square lantern

access.note: Park open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Region of Queens; Rowlett). Beside the Harbour Authority wharf.

events.note: Put in operation 1 April 1899 (Lighthouse Friends, quoting the Department's 1899 report).
Samuel T. Foster appointed keeper 17 February 1899 at $100 a year.
Automated 1 January 1967; the Region says the light changed from red to green that year.
Vinyl siding added; it adorned the walls for several years from 1979.
Given as the decommissioning year by the Region of Queens park page and the Lighthouse Directory. The heritage file and Lighthouse Friends say January 1989.
Coast Guard decided to decommission in January 1989 (heritage file); Lighthouse Friends gives 4 January 1989.
Municipality of Queens bought the lighthouse in July 2000 on behalf of the Medway Area Communities Association.
Moved several metres in late 2001 to allow breakwater restoration.
Port Medway Lighthouse Park officially opened in October 2002.

keepers.name: Samuel T. Foster
keepers.note: Appointed 17 February 1899 at $100 a year (Lighthouse Friends; Department table 1909-10). Lighthouse Friends gives 1919 as the end. The heritage file says there is no record of how long he served. Region: 'Sammy Foster'.

keepers.name: Chelsey Whynot
keepers.note: Named among the lightkeepers on the Region's park page; no dates given.

keepers.name: George McConnell
keepers.note: Started at $150 in 1942; retired 7 October 1959 making $345 (Lighthouse Friends). Heritage file: 1942 to 1959. Called the tower's final formal keeper.

keepers.name: Cecil Earl Dolliver
keepers.note: Caretaker (role recorded as other) after McConnell retired; paid $40 a year until automation on 1 January 1967. Lighthouse Friends: Cecil Dolliver. Heritage file: Cecil Earl Dolliver, the last keeper, caretaker until 1967. The start year is not given by any source; 1959 is McConnell's retirement year.

notes_for_editor: Thin, single-tier station: the four main sources are Lighthouse Friends (which quotes the 1899 report but whose text is not in the local corpus), the Department's keepers' tables, the Municipality's heritage file and the Region's park page. Decommissioning year conflicts: 1987 (Region, Rowlett, station record) against January 1989 (heritage file, Lighthouse Friends). Both are kept and flagged in the story. The Rowlett entry's 1988 start to restoration comes before the 1989 decommissioning date; the story states it as the Directory's date without resolving it. Foster's years: Lighthouse Friends says 1899 to 1919; the heritage file says there is no record of how long he served. The four 'others' after Foster in the heritage file are not all named by any source; only Hopkins, Whynot, McConnell and Dolliver are on the roster. The 1900 Department report list was dropped from the story: its 'February 17, 1899' falls in a date column with no station name beside it in the OCR, so it cannot be matched to Port Medway by row. The 1909-10 keepers' table row is read from one OCR line ('Port Medway Harbour Samuel T. Foster Feb. 17, 1809. . 10) 00'); the year reads 1809 in the OCR. The page image (scan p. 259 of 1911v45i13p21_0744) was viewed at low resolution: the Foster row and a $100 salary were visible, and the year looked like 1899, but it was not confirmed at full resolution, so the story does not rely on the table for the year. The height: Lighthouse Friends says 33 ft to the vane; Rowlett says about 8.5 m (28 ft); the story gives the Department's 33 ft only, and height_m is left out of the story. The range 'visible 6 miles' is taken from the 1899 report as Lighthouse Friends quotes it; the unit is not stated. The Region's 'red to green' change in 1967 is recorded in the characteristic field as the Region's claim only. Not checked: the Coast Guard list of lights for a current status (the light is inactive); whether any keeper other than Foster served before 1919. Port Medway's older headland light (Medway Head) is a separate station, with its own story in the existing archive (ca-ns-medway-head). Position: the record's OSM point (44.132756, -64.575175) sits about 75 m from the Region's GPS figure (44.13208, -64.574547). The record was not changed; a human should check which point marks the tower.
